primary_diagnosis_treated: Mixed diabetic and hypertensive chronic kidney disease (CKD stage 3b)

medications.dose: Start 2.5 mg PO once daily; titrate by 2.5 mg every 2‑4 weeks to target BP <130/80 mmHg, max 10 mg daily
medications.purpose: Renoprotective and antihypertensive therapy for CKD with albuminuria/hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & K⁺ after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends dapagliflozin 10 mg for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (TA775)

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 500 mg PO twice daily (dose‑reduced for eGFR 30‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 permits metformin with dose reduction when eGFR 30‑45; stop if eGFR <30

medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if target BP not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends additional antihypertensive agents when BP remains >130/80 mmHg

medications.dose: Current regimen as prescribed by diabetes team
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management guideline; essential for glucose control

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased glucosuria from dapagliflozin can cause hypoglycaemia when combined with insulin
interactions_checked.action: Reduce insulin dose by 10‑20 % and monitor capillary glucose closely for the first 2 weeks

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention (NG203 contraindicated drugs)
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury (NG203 contraindicated drugs)
contraindications.alternative: Use only one agent (Ramipril) as planned

treatment_summary: Start renoprotective ACE‑I (ramipril) and SGLT2‑i (dapagliflozin) together with a statin (atorvastatin) to address CKD progression and cardiovascular risk per NICE NG203. Add metformin at a reduced dose for additional glycaemic control, and plan amlodipine if blood pressure remains above target after ACE‑I titration. Insulin therapy continues as already prescribed. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, blood pressure, and glucose closely, and avoid chronic NSAIDs and ACE‑I/ARB combination. Follow NICE monitoring intervals and review annually.
